'It's an overseas platform, so the tax office won't find out.' This is the most common misunderstanding about affiliate income from overseas FX such as XM, and it is a dangerous assumption. The National Tax Agency actively conducts audits of individuals who trade over the internet and of individuals who invest overseas. Overseas FX affiliate income falls into both. In addition, when remittances above a certain amount arrive from overseas into a Japanese account, the financial institution files an overseas remittance report with the tax office. Moreover, overseas FX affiliate income is more complicated to process than ordinary affiliate income: (1) USD rewards are converted into yen at the rate on the day they arise; (2) the rate difference up to the payment date is handled separately as foreign exchange gain/loss; (3) revenue is recorded in the year the reward was confirmed, not the payment date. In this video I summarized the points that are easy to get wrong about taxes on overseas FX affiliate income. It also touches on the treatment of XM bonuses and points. If your rewards have been growing, please watch!

Trading gold on an XM KIWAMI account at 1 lot with 100,000 yen, a stop-out occurs after about $5.5 of adverse movement, so I had Gemini verify against IC and EBC. I thought IC would be the cheapest, but never expected EBC to win outright. EBC fixes leverage at 500x unless it's a special time such as before the weekend close. IC has HMR (margin rule), but it isn't as frequent as Exness, where leverage gets restricted before you notice. I'm concerned about EBC's recent blunder of being expelled from the Financial Commission. IC's weak points are deposits/withdrawals and support. [Corrected comparison table of effective drawdown tolerance and cost (100 oz / 15,000 yen = $1 conversion)] Accounts compared: (1) XM KIWAMI; (2) IC Markets (Raw/MT); (3) IC Markets (cTrader); (4) EBC Financial (PRO). Account funds: XM and IC are 100,000 yen at 1000x leverage; EBC is 500x leverage so 200,000 yen is assumed. Stop-loss (SL rate): XM 20% (9,000 yen remaining); both IC accounts 50% (22,500 yen remaining); EBC 30% (27,000 yen remaining). Initial trading cost (spread + commission): (1) about $1.50 (about 2,250 yen); (2) about $1.20 (about 1,800 yen); (3) about $1.10 (about 1,650 yen); (4) about $0.80 (about 1,200 yen). Effective tolerable loss (balance - cost - SL amount): (1) 88,750 yen; (2) 75,700 yen; (3) 75,850 yen; (4) 171,800 yen. Effective tolerable price range: (1) about $5.91 (measured $5.5-5.6); (2) about $5.04; (3) about $5.05; (4) about $11.45. Total round-trip cost per lot: (1) about $15.00 (2,250 yen); (2) about $12.00 (1,800 yen); (3) about $11.00 (1,650 yen); (4) about $8.00 (1,200 yen). Comparison of tolerance per account (with XM as the baseline): XM (100k / 1,000x / SL 20%) - effective tolerance about $5.5 to 5.9. Because you start in the minus by the spread the moment you enter, it falls short of the theoretical value ($6.07) and is stopped out near $5.5. IC Markets (100k / 1,000x / SL 50%) - effective tolerance about $4.7 to 5.0. Because the stop-out level is a high 50% (a balance of 22,500 yen is required), after deducting spread and commission it goes 0.8-0.9 dollars earlier than XM (below $5 to right around $5). It doesn't hold even $5.5, let alone $6. EBC Financial (200k / 500x / SL 30%) - effective tolerance about $11.0 to 11.4. Leverage drops to 500x (required margin 90,000 yen), but the advantage of raising funds to 200,000 yen is very large. The extremely narrow spread/commission cost (about $0.80) also contributes, and it can withstand about twice XM (the $11 range). Difference in total cost (per entry): EBC Pro about $8.00 (almost half of XM); IC cTrader about $11.00; IC Raw (MT4/5) about $12.00; XM KIWAMI about $15.00. For high-leverage, short-range scalping or tight fund management, the picture is 'XM, which can hold on to the limit with SL 20%' versus 'EBC, which withstands $11 with 200,000 yen funds while keeping trading costs lowest'.

Hmmm. Why are the X 'early-call' accounts all counter-trend rebound-hunting scalpers? Occasionally there are trend followers, like the dog teacher, but that's on demo. It doesn't really matter whether it's demo or real as long as there's something to learn from the analysis. But scalping isn't suited to early calls, is it? Often the take-profit timing lasts only an instant, and being told it afterwards in an X post doesn't help. In the first place, there's the problem that too many chicks try to win just by finding early-call accounts and riding along - that's really impossible. Rather than riding X early calls, you'd be better off entrusting your money to a strategy provider who has run an XM copy-trade account at about 5% monthly for over a year.

I underpaid a deposit at XM and it was refunded, but nearly 10,000 yen had been deducted. I've gone back and forth with support many times - can such a thing really happen? The representative's answer: 'When a crypto deposit is refunded, the following two fees are charged and adjusted. Refund processing fee: a fixed fee applied to refunds. This fee is not affected by exchange-rate fluctuations. Network fee: a small blockchain network fee (gas) required to process the on-chain refund transaction. The network fee is variable and updated weekly.' I received it in BNB, and the network fee would be a few hundred yen at most. That means the 'refund fee' must have taken over 9,000 yen, which I think normally can't happen... Also, there were cases where the deposit amount matched exactly yet was somehow treated as an underpayment, which is not good. It may be anti-money-laundering measures, but I wish they'd stop fixing the deposit amount so rigidly. Is XM the only one this fussy?

Couldn't sleep, so I was playing FX police on X and tried out whether P/L and positions can be altered with AI. As a test, I shorted just 0.01 gold at XM and 5 USD/JPY at Hirose, and asked the AI to create the screenshots - done in 30 seconds. I could change the lots and P/L easily lol. FX beginners: only trust accounts that post at entry and then really are winning. P/L and lots can be fabricated easily. But no matter how much you rely on AI, it can't foresee market moves. Wipe out all the accounts pretending to win that have been increasing a lot recently.

Long time no see at this late hour. Several people have worried about me via LINE and DMs, so this is a quick report that I'm alive. Since my last post, my health suddenly went bad - or rather my mental state - and I'm repeating work -> sleep -> work -> sleep; my search for a side job isn't progressing properly and I'm just enduring while time passes. I've said it many times, but the moment I could no longer do FX I stopped even dreaming, and my thoughts only go in a bad direction about how to get through the current hell. The damage from Claude telling me clearly 'Please recognize that even if you live a normal life, you can definitely not return to your original life' was big lol. If things go properly, I'd have to keep paying nearly 400,000 yen every month for at least 5 years to finally get back to break-even. Zero savings in my late 40s... what about the children's school fees? When I casually look again at the stocks, mutual funds and so on I used to hold, they've all more than doubled, so I start thinking that if I had just kept the lifestyle of about 10 years ago I might have had assets of 100 million yen by now - it's just a period where my depression accelerates. For now, XM seems to be running a 100% bonus, so once I have money I have no choice but to take that challenge... but first I need to get my mental state in order... that's about where I am. That said, I have payments again tomorrow, and if I miss it my commuter IC card will stop! If I don't put money in the bank by 19:00 today, the 13th, it's over! What is this life! Let me reincarnate!!! ... Yes, so I'll somehow do my best. Honestly this is a life lived only to repay money... I want a comeback chance. Followers, let's all do our best too. It's tough...
